name: Painterlily
body:
Long ago, there lived a powerful and wicked dungeon-dwelling wizard, master of a menagerie of colorful paint golems and ink elementals, and yet cursed with terrible loneliness. The wizard longed for a companion—someone who would never reject him, never wrinkle his clothes, never fail to keep him entertained. And so the wizard sought out and kidnapped the greatest artist in the land, a gnome painter known for her innovative portraits. He took the gnome to his castle and commanded the gnome to create the image of a humanoid of perfect beauty, perfect dress, and one or two memorable quirks to keep them interesting.

The painter slaved for many months before producing one such painting. Without waiting, the wizard brought it into his laboratory and cast a spell, animating the portrait into a semblance of sentience. But something had gone wrong. This construct had a personality—and not one totally dedicated to the wizard’s whims. The wizard trapped it in his boiling vat of pigments, declaring it a failure, and demanded the gnome try again. And again. As attempt after attempt failed, the painter grew weaker and weaker, and the wizard grew more and more angry.

At last, after one particular creation outright attempted to murder him to gain its freedom, the enraged wizard grabbed the gnome and sealed her in the vat, heedless of her screams.

Inside the vat, the pigments roiled. Over the next few days, the paints boiled and bubbled over the edges of the vat, pooling and drying on the stone floor, splattering onto the walls. These paint golems, created for simple entertainment, became infused with droplets of the gnome’s own colorful personality. And they were angry. The next time the wizard returned to his laboratory, he did not come out again.

Physical Description: Painterlilies are two-dimensional beings. If viewed from the side, they resemble nothing but a haze of thin lines. They look rather like cartoonish drawings of humans, with enormous eyes, small noses, and extremely colorful hair, eyes and clothing. Some have compared them to walking bas-reliefs of human-sized gnomes. They have waifish forms, standing around five feet in height, but some are quite tall or bulky. Despite being almost devoid of mass, painterlilies’s nevertheless weigh about 150 pounds – a paradox that puzzled their creator. All painterlilies possess the image of a white lily somewhere on them, either as a clothing motif, a tattoo, or an accessory of some kind (the signature of their painter).

Society: After escaping the wizard’s dungeon, the painterlilies largely dispersed, each seeking to explore the strange new world—a much more dimensional land than their cramped cauldron. They only very rarely congregate, gathering in old ruins and cathedrals for mutual protection.

Relations: Painterlilies are described by all species except gnomes as being exceptionally gnomelike—and indeed, they are eccentrics full of energetic movement and manner. But gnomes are disturbed by painterlilies, who seem “too lifelike” to them. The sentiment, however, is not mutual: Painterlilies feel very strong kinship with gnomes, and tend to follow them around everywhere. Painterlilies love the creativity of dwarves, and some take up work in forges and smithies, helping to craft new forms of art both beautiful and practical. Beings of titanic personality, painterlilies have trouble getting along with most humanoids. Halflings find painterlilies adorable, and vice versa.

Alignment and Religion: Painterlilies tend towards erratic, unreliable modes of behavior, but almost always seek to do what is best for all involved. They are usually chaotic good. They look favorably on gnome deities and deities of art and beauty.

Adventurers: Painterlilies are natural-born wanderers. The only way to create more of their kind is to gather exotic pigments and paint a new being. These pigments cannot be purchased—they only seem to work if the painterlily has traveled enough to obtain them itself. It is the journey, not the paint, that truly matters. Painterlilies can use mud and charcoal to paint their own kind, provided the materials are gathered over the course of an epic quest. Of course, some painterlilies just travel due to their natural curiosity and wonder at the world. Painterlies have difficulties gauging when they’re in over their heads, and so make for natural adventurers.

Core Traits (16 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Painterlilies are lithe with powerful personalities, but are otherwise thin and foolish. They gain +2 Charisma, +2 Dexterity, –2 Constitution, and –2 Wisdom. –1 RP
Size: Painterlilies are Medium and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
Type: Painterlilies are half-constructs. 7 RP
Speed: Painterlilies have a base land speed of 30 feet. They also have a climb speed of 20 feet. 2 RP
Languages: Painterlilies begin play speaking Common and Gnome. Painterlilies with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Dwarven, Giant, Goblin, Halfling, Orc, and Sylvan.
Other Traits
Lucky: Painterlilies gain a +2 luck bonus on all saving throws. 4 RP
Two-Dimensional: Painterlilies are almost entirely two-dimensional and extremely thin from the side view. A painterlily can choose to turn itself as a move action, choosing two opposite edges of its space. It gains concealment against attacks that enter through either of these edges, and it cannot make attacks through those edges. This lasts until the painterlily moves, or turns itself again. Equipment and armor worn by a painterlily flattens to conform to their unique dimensions (though it does not otherwise resize or change). 3 RP
Meld with Surface: As a full-round action, a painterlily can merge with the touched surface of stone, wood, paper, metal, or similar material large enough to depict its entire form. The surface need not be perfectly regular, but should be no rougher than tree bark. It can merge with a ceiling in this way, if within reach, but merging with a horizontal surface treats the painterlily as though prone. This otherwise functions as meld into stone with no duration limit, but the painterlily can only travel along the surface (using their climb speed) and not through the object. While merged, the painterlily can see what is going on around it, and is still visible on the surface, resembling a painted image or bas-relief. A melded painterlily is unable to turn itself using the two-dimentional trait. A melded painterlily may be targeted as normal. The painterlily is expelled if it falls unconscious, or if the surface is destroyed. 4 RP
Squeeze Through Cracks: Painterlilies squeeze through slits of any thickness without making an Escape Artist check, provided the slit is at least as tall or wide as they are. 1 RP
Thin as Paper: Painterlilies are treated as Fine-sized creatures (-8) for purposes of CMB and CMD checks and for determining the effects of wind. –2 RP
Vulnerability to Water: Painterlilies do not need to drink, and in fact, many liquids are dangerous to them. Most liquids (water, ale, potions) function as a flask of acid against them, blurring and smudging their lines (1d6 damage). Full immersion in such a liquid likewise damages them as though it were acid (10d6 damage per round). More viscous fluids, like honey, do not damage them. Painterlilies cannot safely consume potions, but they can purchase potions in pigment form at 125% the normal price. These paints can be applied safely. –2 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing painterlily traits.

Beloved By All: Not all painterlilies are wont to avoid the spotlight. Some are almost obnoxiously good at getting people to like them—even people who by all logic shouldn’t. These painterlilies gain a +4 racial bonus on Diplomacy checks. In addition, whenever they use Diplomacy to shift a creature’s attitude, they can do so up to three steps rather than just two. This trait replaces meld with surface.
Burnt Lily: Some younger painterlilies are in fact not made of paint at all, but charcoal and ash. These painterlilies gain fire resistance 5, but are much less stable: Any damage to them inflicted by liquids via the vulnerability to water trait is increased by +50%.
Catch the Wind: Some painterlilies are exceptionally thin, but lack the ability to easily slide across surfaces. These painterlilies take no damage from falling (as if subject to a constant non-magical feather fall spell). Painterlilies with this racial trait do not gain a climb speed.
Retouch Self: Some painterlilies intensively study how to use paints to modify their own forms. These painterlilies can, with a set of special paints costing 200 gp, take 10 minutes to modify their form to gain any single benefit that could be conferred by beast shape I (including the ability score bonus, but not including the size change or actual transformation). This benefit lasts 1 hour, after which the paints fade and peel away. Painterlilies with this racial trait do not gain the meld with surface trait.
Misfortune Magnet: Some Painterlilies seem almost cursed to misfortune, but they have developed their own strange ways of bouncing back from injury. Painterlilies with this alternate trait gain fast healing 1 while at negative or 0 hit points. Painterlilies with this racial trait do not gain the lucky trait.

Seven Bizarre Races Copyright 2025 Zenith Games Author Author: Nikolai Geier
